ref_text.narrator: Twelve hundred years ago, they did not build a temple. They carved one, out of a living mountain.

voices.narrator_epic: male, middle-aged, very low pitch, british accent

jobs.text: They carved it... out of one single rock.
And they started from the roof. Not the floor.
One wrong hit could ruin everything. Watch how they did it.
This is the Kailasa Temple, at the Ellora Caves, in Maharashtra, India.
Ellora has thirty-four caves, cut into one long cliff. Kailasa is cave sixteen.
It was carved around the year seven hundred and sixty, under King Krishna the First.
Step one. Workers cut three deep trenches into the hill.
That left one giant block of rock, standing alone.
Step two. They started at the top, and carved downwards.
First the roof. Then the walls. Then the floor.
No machines. Only hammers and chisels.
They removed about two hundred thousand tonnes of stone.
The temple is about thirty-two metres tall. As high as a ten-storey building.
Pillars, stairs, bridges, even life-size elephants. All one piece of rock.
One wrong strike... and the stone could never be put back.
Today, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Still standing, after twelve hundred years.
Comment ROCK if this amazed you. And follow for the next build.
